title: EasySSH protocol
description: Entities (v1 shapes), envelopes and the starting command/event set.

shell_integration.description: Opt-in shell integration: after the shell starts, the daemon sends a small script that reports prompts, working directory and exit codes through OSC 6973. Absent means off.

Connection.description: A saved host. Rust: domain::Connection. `proxy_jump` is the v1 jump host (OpenSSH ProxyJump spec).

Group.description: Rust: domain::Group. `parent_id` has serde(default), so it is optional.

Workspace.description: files/snippets/forwarding are legacy values kept so schema 5 metadata still deserializes.

crash_reports.description: null until the user answered the first-run question.

TelemetryPreferences.description: Rust: domain::TelemetryPreferences. Both fields have serde(default).

schema_version.description: Storage schema of the v1 config file (AppConfig::SCHEMA_VERSION, 7). Unrelated to the protocol SchemaVersion.

ssh_engine.description: Absent means russh (the built-in engine); openssh only when the user chose it.

AppConfig.description: The v1 configuration file. Fields with serde(default) in Rust (tunnels, terminal, sessions, transfer_history, workspace, display_density, sidebar, sync, experimental, telemetry) are optional here; v1 always writes them.

SchemaVersion.description: Protocol schema version. Additive changes only within a version.

ProtoError.description: Machine-readable code plus a human message.

payload.description: Shape depends on `kind`; see the *Params definitions.
Shape depends on `kind`; see the *Event definitions.

Reply.description: Answer to the Command with the same id: exactly one of `ok` or `error`.

ok.description: Result payload; shape depends on the command kind.

schema_version.description: The protocol schema version the client speaks. A daemon that speaks another version answers with the `schema_mismatch` error.

app_version.description: Build version of the client application. The app compares the daemon's `app_version` with its own and asks a daemon from another build to drain (`daemon.shutdown_when_idle`).

ProtoHelloParams.description: Command `proto.hello` payload. Reply: ProtoHelloResult, or the error `schema_mismatch`.

schema_version.description: The protocol schema version the daemon speaks.

app_version.description: Build version of the daemon (the application executable it runs from).

draining.description: True once the daemon was asked to exit when its sessions end; it refuses new sessions.

group.description: A group to create when no group with this id exists yet; `connection.group_id` may refer to it.

group_path.description: Folders from the root, outermost first.

identity_file.description: Key file path the source referenced; never read.

openssh_only.description: Reasons the host needs the OpenSSH engine.

tags.description: Tags to put on the host (service imports bring the service's own).

source.description: Stable key of the host at its origin (service imports, for example `control:https://panel.example.com#12`). A later import of the same key updates the host it created, even when its address changed.

exists.description: Preview only: a stored host has the same hostname, port and user. Ignored by hosts.import_apply.

problem.description: Preview only: why the host cannot be imported. Ignored by hosts.import_apply.

ImportHost.description: A host found in an import file. Never carries a secret.

path.description: File read by the daemon (use for large files; at most 8 MiB). Exactly one of `path` and `data`.

data.description: The file's bytes, base64. Exactly one of `path` and `data`; the frame limit (4 MiB) applies.

file_name.description: Name of the file, for formats that name a session after it.

base_dir.description: Directory OpenSSH `Include` paths resolve in and may not leave. Only for the user's own `~/.ssh`, on their explicit action.

HostsImportPreviewParams.description: Command `hosts.import_preview` payload. Reply: HostsImportPreviewResult. Writes nothing.

removed.description: Service imports: names of stored hosts an earlier import created that the service no longer lists. Nothing is removed.

ImportDuplicatePolicy.description: What to do with an imported host that matches a stored one (same hostname, port and user).

ImportGroupMode.description: `source`: the file's folders (stored groups of the same name are reused). `none`: no group for new hosts. `existing`: every host goes into `group_id`.

HostsImportApplyParams.description: Command `hosts.import_apply` payload. Reply: HostsImportApplyResult. Adds and updates only; nothing stored is ever removed. Broadcasts `hosts.changed` when something changed.

host.description: The host pattern as stored: a name, `[host]:port`, a comma list, or a `|1|salt|hash` digest when `hashed`.

KnownHostEntry.description: A stored known_hosts entry. The key itself is not sent, only its fingerprint.

path.description: Path of an OpenSSH known_hosts file, read by the daemon. The client picks it (normally `~/.ssh/known_hosts`).

skipped.description: Lines that could not be read.

KnownHostsRemoveParams.description: Command `known_hosts.remove` payload. Reply: null. Removing an unknown id is not an error.

ssh_auth_sock.description: The client's current SSH_AUTH_SOCK, so the session uses the agent of the user's current login. Must be an absolute path to a socket owned by the daemon's user; otherwise it is ignored. Ignored on Windows.

SessionOpenParams.description: Command `session.open` payload. host_id null opens a local shell. Reply: SessionOpenResult.

engine.description: The engine the session runs on; absent for a local shell.

engine_reason.description: Why that engine was chosen, in English, for display in a tooltip.

exit_code.description: Set once the session has ended; null while running or when the status is unknown.

first_seq.description: Offset of the oldest output still buffered.

next_seq.description: Offset the next output will have (total bytes produced).

engine.description: The engine the session runs on; absent for a local shell.

engine_reason.description: Why that engine was chosen, in English, for display in a tooltip.

SessionInfo.description: A session the daemon holds. Ended sessions stay listed (with their scrollback) until `session.close`.

path.description: Pass it as `port` of a serial host.

description.description: What the OS knows: the USB product and vendor, or the kind of port.

SerialPortInfo.description: A serial port the OS lists.

SerialPortsParams.description: Command `serial.ports` payload: list the serial ports of this machine. Reply: SerialPortsResult.

from_seq.description: Replay output from this offset; omitted means everything still buffered.

SessionAttachParams.description: Command `session.attach` payload. Subscribes this connection to the session's output and exit events: the reply comes first, then the buffered output from `from_seq` as `session.output` events, then (if the session already ended) `session.exit`, then live events. Attaching again replaces the earlier subscription of the same connection. Reply: SessionAttachResult.

first_seq.description: Offset of the oldest output still buffered.

next_seq.description: Offset the next output will have.

truncated.description: True when output before the first replayed byte was dropped (`from_seq`, or the start of the stream, fell before `first_seq`).

SessionDetachParams.description: Command `session.detach` payload. Stops this connection's events for the session; the session keeps running. Reply: null.

remember.description: Save the answer in the vault for this host. Only honoured for a prompt the event marked `rememberable`.

AskpassReplyParams.description: Command `askpass.reply` payload. answer null cancels the prompt. Reply: null.

endpoint.description: `<port> <token>` for the `ANIXOPS_SSH_ASKPASS` variable of an OpenSSH child process.

AskpassEndpointResult.description: Secret: it lets a process answer for the daemon's prompts; hand it only to OpenSSH child processes.

seq.description: Offset in bytes of `data` within the session's output stream (UTF-8, as sent). Optional for compatibility; the daemon always sets it. Consecutive events of one session are contiguous unless the buffer dropped output.

SessionOutputEvent.description: Event `session.output` payload. Sent to every client attached to the session, first as replay of the buffered scrollback (from the requested offset), then live.

signal.description: The signal's name without `SIG` (`TERM`), when `reason` is `signal`.

SessionExitEvent.description: Event `session.exit` payload. `reason` and `signal` are optional: daemons before they were added send only the code.

SessionExitReason.description: Why a session ended: the shell exited with `code`, was killed by `signal`, or ended without a status (the connection dropped).

rememberable.description: The prompt asks for the saved password or key passphrase of a saved host: the dialog may offer "Remember in vault".

vault_locked.description: A saved answer exists but the vault is locked: the dialog may offer to unlock it (`askpass.unlock`).

kind.description: What the prompt asks for; absent for OpenSSH's askpass prompts. `security_key_pin` asks for the PIN of a FIDO2 security key; `security_key_touch` only tells the user to touch the key and takes no answer (it closes with `askpass.resolved`).

echo.description: Whether the answer may be shown while typing (keyboard-interactive prompts).

DaemonShutdownWhenIdleParams.description: Command `daemon.shutdown_when_idle` payload. The daemon refuses new sessions (error `draining`) and exits once no session is running, even if clients stay connected. Reply: DaemonShutdownWhenIdleResult.

running_sessions.description: Sessions still running; the daemon exits when this reaches 0.

HostsChangedEvent.description: Event `hosts.changed` payload. Sent to every connected client after `hosts.save`, `hosts.delete` or a `hosts.import_apply` that changed something; clients refresh their host list.

AskpassResolvedEvent.description: Event `askpass.resolved` payload. The prompt `id` was answered, cancelled or timed out; clients close any dialog for it.

unlock_methods.description: Windows Hello, Touch ID: the methods this device can offer to open a passphrase vault. Absent from older daemons.

VaultStatus.description: The vault state. No secret is ever part of it.

available.description: The OS offers it on this device right now. The UI shows the biometric methods only when available; `security_key` is shown disabled with an explanation when it is not.

items.description: The separately removable entries behind the method: the security keys added to the vault. Empty for the other methods. Absent from older daemons.

UnlockMethod.description: A biometric or OS unlock method of the vault.

label.description: The name the user gave the security key.

UnlockItem.description: One removable entry of an unlock method, for example one FIDO2 security key.

VaultUnlockParams.description: Command `vault.unlock` payload. Reply: VaultStatus. Fails with `wrong_passphrase`.

VaultUnlockWithParams.description: Command `vault.unlock_with` payload: open the vault with an enabled unlock method (the system prompt appears). Reply: VaultStatus. Fails with `unlock_cancelled` when the user declines; the passphrase still works.

VaultEnableUnlockParams.description: Command `vault.enable_unlock` payload: turn an unlock method on. The passphrase is needed once; the system asks the user to confirm. Reply: VaultStatus.

VaultDisableUnlockParams.description: Command `vault.disable_unlock` payload: turn an unlock method off and delete its stored key copy. Reply: VaultStatus.

label.description: A name for the key; empty gets a numbered default.

VaultAddUnlockItemParams.description: Command `vault.add_unlock_item` payload: add one entry to an unlock method that holds several (another security key). The passphrase is needed once; the key asks for a touch (and its PIN). Reply: VaultStatus.

VaultRemoveUnlockItemParams.description: Command `vault.remove_unlock_item` payload: remove one entry (one security key) of an unlock method. Reply: VaultStatus.

current.description: Required to change an existing passphrase.

VaultSetPassphraseParams.description: Command `vault.set_passphrase` payload: set the vault passphrase, or change it when `current` is given. Reply: VaultStatus.

VaultRemovePassphraseParams.description: Command `vault.remove_passphrase` payload: go back to keychain-only protection. Reply: VaultStatus.

VaultForgetAllParams.description: Command `vault.forget_all` payload: delete every saved password, key and passphrase. Works while locked. Reply: VaultForgetAllResult.

SecretsStatusParams.description: Command `secrets.status` payload. Reply: SecretsStatusResult. Needs no unlock.

SecretsStatusResult.description: Which secrets a host has saved. Never the values.

password.description: Absent keeps the saved value; an empty string clears it.

private_key.description: Key text (PEM or OpenSSH). Absent keeps; empty clears.

passphrase.description: Key passphrase. Absent keeps; empty clears.

SecretsSetParams.description: Command `secrets.set` payload. Reply: SecretsStatusResult. Fails with `vault_locked` when a passphrase vault is locked.

AskpassUnlockParams.description: Command `askpass.unlock` payload: unlock the vault and answer prompt `id` from it. Reply: null. Fails with `wrong_passphrase`.

AskpassBindParams.description: Command `askpass.bind` payload: tell the daemon that the OpenSSH process using askpass `context` connects to saved host `host_id`, so its password and passphrase prompts for exactly that host and user may be answered from the vault. Reply: null.

AskpassUnbindParams.description: Command `askpass.unbind` payload: the process is over. Reply: null.

VaultChangedEvent.description: Event `vault.changed` payload. Sent to every client when the vault locks or unlocks (also by auto-lock).

SyncState.description: `locked`: signed in, but the vault is locked, so the account secrets cannot be opened yet.

resolved.description: Same-field conflicts a merge decided; the losing value is in the record's history.

SyncCounts.description: What the last sync run did.

fingerprint.description: This account's safety number: twelve groups of five digits. Members compare it with what they see for you.

SyncStatus.description: The sync state. No secret is ever part of it. Reply of `sync.status`, `sync.signup`, `sync.signin`, `sync.signout` and `sync.now`, and payload of event `sync.state`.

server_url.description: https://, or http:// only for a loopback address.

passphrase.description: Stretched on this device with Argon2id; never sent and never stored.

device_name.description: How this device appears in the device list; defaults to the host name.

SyncSignupParams.description: Command `sync.signup` payload: create an account on the server (OPAQUE registration), create the personal vault and enroll this device. Reply: SyncStatus.

server_url.description: https://, or http:// only for a loopback address.

passphrase.description: Stretched on this device with Argon2id; never sent and never stored.

device_name.description: How this device appears in the device list; defaults to the host name.

SyncSigninParams.description: Command `sync.signin` payload: sign in to an existing account on this device (OPAQUE login, unwrap the account keys, enroll this device with an account-signed certificate). Reply: SyncStatus. Fails with `wrong_passphrase`.

SyncSignoutParams.description: Command `sync.signout` payload: end the session, revoke nothing, forget the account keys and sync bookkeeping on this device. Hosts stay. Reply: SyncStatus.

SyncNowParams.description: Command `sync.now` payload: pull and push now. Reply: SyncStatus.

revoked_at.description: Unix seconds on the server's clock; present when revoked. What the device sent before is still valid, what it sends after is refused.

cert_expires_at.description: Unix seconds. The device certificate is renewed automatically while signed in.

SyncDevicesRevokeParams.description: Command `sync.devices.revoke` payload: the server stops accepting pushes from that device and ends its sessions. Reply: null. The current device cannot be revoked.

role.description: The signed-in account's role in a team vault.

VaultCreateSharedParams.description: Command `vault.create_shared` payload: create a team vault on the server; the caller is its owner. Reply: VaultInfo.

fingerprint.description: Safety number of the member's account keys.

trust.description: `confirmed`: a person compared the fingerprint when adding the member; `unconfirmed`: first seen from the server; `changed`: the keys differ from the pinned ones, and this member's records are refused.

VaultMembersLookupParams.description: Command `vault.members.lookup` payload: look an account up and compute its fingerprint, to show before adding. Reply: VaultMembersLookupResult.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint the person compared. The daemon looks the account up again and refuses (`fingerprint_mismatch`) when the keys changed.

VaultMembersAddParams.description: Command `vault.members.add` payload (owner only): seal the vault key to the member and add them. Reply: VaultMember.

VaultMembersRemoveParams.description: Command `vault.members.remove` payload (owner only): removes the member and replaces the vault key, re-encrypting every record under the new one. Reply: null.

HostsMoveVaultParams.description: Command `hosts.move_vault` payload: move a host into another vault. The host gets a new id (a record never changes vault); its tunnels follow. Reply: HostsMoveVaultResult.

HostHistoryEntry.description: A value of one host field that an edit or a merge replaced.

HostsHistoryParams.description: Command `hosts.history` payload. Reply: HostsHistoryResult (newest first; secrets are never listed).

HostsHistoryRestoreParams.description: Command `hosts.history_restore` payload: put one old value back, as an ordinary edit that syncs. Reply: null.

host_vaults.description: Host id to vault id, for the hosts that are not in the personal vault.

SshEngine.description: Rust: domain::SshEngine. The global engine setting, and the engine a session actually runs on.

EnginePreference.description: Rust: domain::EnginePreference. Per-host override of the global engine; `auto` follows the global setting.

HostKeyDecision.description: `replace_and_save` is the only way to accept a changed key; any other answer to a changed key refuses the connection.

expected.description: Fingerprints on record: of the changed key, or of the other key types when the key is of a new type.

HostkeyPromptEvent.description: Event `hostkey.prompt` payload: the engine needs a decision about a host key. Answer with `hostkey.reply`.

HostkeyResolvedEvent.description: Event `hostkey.resolved` payload: the prompt was answered, cancelled or timed out; close its dialog.

EngineConnectionsResult.description: `opened` counts every connection the russh engine has opened since the daemon started.

detail.description: Also list every process's owner, command line and executable.

MonitorSampleParams.description: Command `monitor.sample` payload (russh engine): reads the server's load, memory, network, disks and processes on the connection the terminal already has. Never connects. Reply: MonitorSampleResult.

output.description: What the read-only sample script printed (`@section` markers, raw /proc and df text).

latency_ms.description: Keepalive round trip; null when the server did not answer it.

MonitorSignalParams.description: Command `monitor.signal` payload (russh engine): sends a signal to a process as the login user, on the existing connection.

TransferStartParams.description: Command `transfer.start` payload. Both paths are final (an upload names the remote file, not its directory). Progress and the end arrive as events. Reply: TransferStartResult.

TransferProgressEvent.description: Event `transfer.progress` payload: bytes moved so far.

skipped.description: Links a folder transfer left out: broken, or leading back up into a folder that holds them. Absent when none.

TunnelStartParams.description: Command `tunnel.start` payload (russh engine). Reply: TunnelStartResult; later changes arrive as `tunnel.status`.

TunnelStateName.description: `reconnecting`: the connection dropped; the forward is closed while a new connection is made (the reason is in `error`).

channel_errors.description: Connections the running forward accepted but could not pass on (the server refused the channel, the target is down). Optional; absent means none.

last_channel_error.description: Why the last of `channel_errors` failed, e.g. `127.0.0.1:1: connect failed`.

channel_errors.description: Connections the running forward accepted but could not pass on (the server refused the channel, the target is down). Optional; absent means none.

last_channel_error.description: Why the last of `channel_errors` failed, e.g. `127.0.0.1:1: connect failed`.
